title: Investigating Industrial Process Conditions on PAH Emission from Carbonaceous Materials
author: Jakovljevic, Aarhaug, et al.

steps.title: Clean all apparatus
steps.instruction: Mechanically brush steel crucible and lid, wash them with acetone, then heat in a muffle furnace to 650 °C in air and hold for 30–45 min (Setup 1). Wash steel tube and boat with acetone and heat the tube furnace to 1300 °C in synthetic air for 30 min (Setup 2). Rinse all glass bottles, Teflon tubes and small steel connectors with fresh 2‑propanol before use.

steps.title: Prepare cryostat and load sample
steps.instruction: Turn on the cryostat and set the temperature to –10 °C. While the cryostat stabilises, weigh the pre‑set mass of the representative carbon material at room temperature and place it in the crucible (Setup 1) or steel boat (Setup 2). Insert the crucible/boat into the corresponding furnace, connect it to the emission sampling system and verify that no gas leaks are present.

steps.title: Record initial sample mass
steps.instruction: Weigh the carbon material sample at room temperature before starting the temperature program and record the mass.

steps.title: Arrange washing bottles for Phase I
steps.instruction: Set up three washing bottles (Set#1) filled with 2‑propanol to capture PAHs released during Phase I (room temperature → 400 °C).

steps.title: Run Phase I temperature program
steps.instruction: Ramp the furnace temperature from room temperature to 400 °C at 6 °C min⁻¹ for Setup 1 or 5 °C min⁻¹ for Setup 2, then hold at 400 °C for 1 h.

steps.title: Collect Phase I solvent and clean tube
steps.instruction: After the 1 h hold, remove Set#1, seal the bottles and send the solvent and washing liquids for analysis. Replace the bottles with a clean Set#2 containing fresh 2‑propanol, and flush the connecting tube with a small amount of fresh 2‑propanol.

steps.title: Arrange washing bottles for Phase II
steps.instruction: Place a fresh set of three washing bottles (Set#2) for Phase II (401 °C → 750 °C).

steps.title: Run Phase II temperature program
steps.instruction: Ramp the temperature from 401 °C to 750 °C (ramp rate as used for Phase I) and hold at 750 °C for the prescribed time (as defined in the experimental design).

steps.title: Collect Phase II solvent and clean tube
steps.instruction: After Phase II, remove the bottles, seal the solvents for analysis, replace with a clean Set#3 of washing bottles, and again flush the tube with fresh 2‑propanol.

steps.title: Arrange washing bottles for Phase III
steps.instruction: Place the final set of three washing bottles (Set#3) for Phase III (751 °C → 1100 °C).

steps.title: Run Phase III temperature program
steps.instruction: Ramp the temperature from 751 °C to 1100 °C (same ramp rate as earlier phases) and hold at 1100 °C for the prescribed time.

steps.title: Collect Phase III solvent
steps.instruction: After the Phase III hold, remove Set#3, seal the bottles and send all three sets of solvents (Phase I‑III) for analysis.

steps.title: Record final sample mass
steps.instruction: Weigh the carbon material again at room temperature after the experiment to determine total mass loss.

steps.title: Combine and store solvent extracts
steps.instruction: For each experiment, combine the 2‑propanol from the two last washing bottles with a small volume of fresh 2‑propanol used for washing all three bottles, yielding a single fluid sample of 220 mL–280 mL. Transfer the combined extract to a glass bottle, wrap it in aluminum foil, and refrigerate at +4 °C until GC‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Submit samples for GC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Add an internal standard containing deuterated PAH congeners to each combined extract. Perform liquid‑liquid extraction with solvent exchange to cyclohexane, clean up using the Grimmer method followed by a deactivated silica column (adsorption chromatography). Analyse the cleaned extract by GC‑MS (Agilent 7890A GC with 5977A MSD or equivalent) using selected‑ion monitoring (SIM) as described in Table 2.

steps.title: Optional empty‑furnace blank test
steps.instruction: To assess baseline contamination, run three consecutive experiments with no carbon sample in the furnace. Apply the standard cleaning procedure before the first run and between runs, use an Argon atmosphere, do not change the washing bottles between temperature phases, and collect a single solvent sample at the end of each run for PAH analysis.
